validator: Validator role (crypto-autoresearcher agents/validator.md), Claude Opus 5.5 subagent. Not the producer of the runs, but launched from the producing Claude Code session (finding F11).
method: Every headline number was recomputed in Python (standard library) from the 126 raw ic price outputs and isolation.jsonl, without summary.json's values, summarise.sh or jq. Per process: the median over its 3 repetitions of phases_ns.collect and of total_ns. Per round: a/c (A/B) and a/q (A/A). A round is kept only if all three isolation records (last per label) have contended false and exit_status 0. Statistic: the median of the per-round ratios, with a percentile bootstrap over rounds implemented from PROTOCOL.md and ../summarise.sh's definition: 2000 resamples of 42 indices drawn consecutively from s <- (1103515245 s + 12345) mod 2^31, seed 20261029, index s mod 42, in ascending round order, sorted resample medians [50] and [1949]. The generator is evaluated in two ways: as jq executes it (IEEE-754 double multiply and add, truncation before mod), which reproduces every claim bit for bit, and as an exact integer LCG, which does not (findings F1-F3). A large Mersenne-Twister bootstrap gives an unbiased reference. Decision rule: A/B lo > 1 and A/B lo > A/A hi, per metric. Second pass: the corrected intervals of summary-corrected.json were recomputed for both sessions with the validator's own Python. The definitions are those of correct_bootstrap.sh and ../summarise.sh (2026-10-23: A/B = baseline-rN / candidate-rN of runs/time/ab for N = 1..30 in that order; A/A = runs/time/aa baseline-r(2k-1) / baseline-r(2k), k = 1..5; seed 20261023. 2026-10-29: A/B = a/c, A/A = a/q per round, rounds 1..42; seed 20261029. Per process: the median of the 3 repetitions. 2000 resamples of n consecutive draws, index s mod n, sorted medians [50] and [1949].). The corrected intervals come from an exact integer LCG; the as-run ones come from the double-rounded step. All 76 published values, including medians, counts, the odd-round shares, margins and flags, agree bit for bit. correct_bootstrap.sh was read but not executed.
status_basis: Second pass. 'pass' means: every as-run number in summary.json (34 entries) and every value in summary-corrected.json for both sessions (76 entries) recomputes exactly from the repository raw data with the validator's own code; every control holds; the counters replay identically and the recovered logarithm is verified (replay-certificate.json, unchanged). The corrected publications read accurately: the aa2 README, CORRECTION.md, report.typ/pdf, the plots and the leaderboard builder (F1-F4 and F9 resolved). That includes the 'marginal (+0.005), not claimed' handling of the whole set-up. Still open, neither changing a number or verdict: the committed board renders predate the corrected builder and must be regenerated before the section is shown (F14), and the first session's README and report should point to the correction (F15). A pass does not admit an ECDLP or rho-gap change: no counted cost moves (F12).

exact_lcg_parity_stratification.why: mod 2^31 with odd increment and odd multiplier, the LCG's lowest bit alternates, so s mod n (n even) alternates parity

findings: F1 (material: the bootstrap generator). summarise.sh, and ../summarise.sh, step s <- (s*1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648 in jq, which computes in IEEE-754 doubles. s*1103515245 exceeds 2^53 from the first step and is rounded before '%'. jq 1.7 here gives the states 178439288, 200959840, 962425888, ... where the integer LCG gives 178439290, 260506667, 1677987976, .... The rounded sequence loses low-order bits, enters a cycle of period 10466 after 7066 steps, and is almost always even. Because n = 42 is even, s mod 42 is then almost always even. Over the 84,000 draws, each odd-numbered round is drawn 3728 to 4333 times and each even-numbered round 1 to 40 times; uniform sampling would give about 2000 each. The 'median with a 95% percentile bootstrap over rounds' is therefore in effect a bootstrap over the 21 odd rounds. Those are exactly the rounds on permutations aqc, qac and caq, so it also loses the balance the schedule was built for: over those rounds a runs before c in two permutations of three, against one of three over the even rounds. The claimed numbers reproduce bit for bit under the as-executed semantics (headline rel_diff 0). They do not reproduce under the textbook integer LCG with the same constants and seed, which is the plain reading of 'the same LCG'.

F2 (the intervals under a correct bootstrap; the same 42 per-round ratios). Unbiased reference, 400,000 Mersenne-Twister resamples: collect A/B [1.0677, 1.1365] (claimed [1.0898, 1.1597]); collect A/A [0.9769, 1.0254] (claimed [0.9771, 1.0297]); whole set-up A/B [1.0204, 1.0824] (claimed [1.0205, 1.1159]); whole set-up A/A [0.9459, 1.0149] (claimed [0.9409, 1.0354]). The integer LCG with the protocol's seed agrees with the reference within resampling noise (collect A/B [1.0677, 1.1358]). The claimed collect A/B interval excludes everything below 1.0898, although the reference lower end is 1.0677.

F3 (do the decisions survive a correct bootstrap?). Collect phase: established as executed, under the integer LCG, and in 500 of 500 independent Mersenne-Twister seeds × 2000 resamples (A/B lower end 1.0661 to 1.0681 against A/A upper end 1.0251 to 1.0274). The collect-phase claim is robust to F1. Whole set-up: not established as executed, but established under the integer LCG (1.0204 > 1.0156) and in 98.4% of the MT seeds (A/B lower end 1.0204 against A/A upper end 1.0149, a margin of about 0.005). The pre-registered rule as executed says 'not established', and switching generators after seeing the data would be a post-hoc re-analysis, so this report does not turn the whole set-up into a claim. The study's stated reason, '1.021 is below the A/A's 1.035', rests on an A/A upper end that a correct bootstrap puts at 1.015.

F4 (the README explains the asymmetric A/B interval wrongly). The README says 'The A/B interval is lopsided because the per-round ratios cluster just above the median'. The asymmetry is F1: the odd-round collect A/B median is 1.1371 and the even-round median is 1.0719, and the interval brackets the odd-round median. Under a correct bootstrap the interval is roughly symmetric about 1.093 ([1.068, 1.136]). 'Its lower end still clears the A/A upper end by 0.06' is true only of the as-executed numbers; the reference margin is 1.0677 - 1.0254 = 0.042.

F5 (first session; the published board section). The same defect affects the first session's 30-round A/B intervals in ../summarise.sh: odd rounds were drawn about 3760 to 4160 times and even rounds 7 to 37. Arm order alternated each round in that session, so its effective resample came from rounds of a single arm order. With my own code and the same generator I reproduce its collect A/B [1.0648, 1.1604] and whole set-up A/B [1.0179, 1.0685]. A correct bootstrap gives [1.0821, 1.1492] and [1.0179, 1.0798]. Its 5-pair A/A (odd n) is not hit by the parity collapse, and its 'not established' verdict is unchanged (A/A upper end 1.087 > 1.082). Commit 5190fd62d, which landed during this validation, adds docs/ic/LEADERBOARD.md section 'Aimed-subset gather in relation collection, outside tables A–C'. It prints both sessions' intervals as 'median [95% bootstrap]'. Per git grep at HEAD over *.sh and *.jq, only these two scripts use this LCG. Recommendation, for the Coordinator to decide: show the intervals labelled as the declared jq-LCG interval (odd rounds only), or publish corrected intervals as an explicitly post-hoc re-analysis, and fix the generator in integer arithmetic before reusing it.

F6 (A/A design). The A/A ratio a/q and the A/B ratio a/c share the numerator a, so the two intervals the rule compares are correlated, and the rule compares interval endpoints rather than testing a difference. It was pre-registered, and it errs toward not claiming, so this is a note, not a defect. Per-process medians: q's collect, 235.2 ms, is 2.1% above a's, 230.3 ms; the per-round A/A median is 0.9994.

F7 (route: local, not Iso Lab). The deviation from the EKS default (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md §9a) is declared in PROTOCOL.md before measurement, with a concrete reason: the reachable EKS paths run ecbench specs only, the three processes of a round need one host, and isolab_k8s_run needs an MCP this container lacks. The consequence is a single shared session container: 4 logical CPUs, CPU 3 reserved for the process, the agent's own processes (claude, git) on the others. 71 launches were refused for CPU pressure. All 126 admitted processes were uncontended: other_cpu_seconds at most 0.19 s against about 1.6 s of wall time, and 428 to 455 involuntary switches. No SMT-sibling or frequency control is recorded. My replays ran sequentially on the same container class (kernel 6.18.44-fc-v185, the same /tmp binaries) without isolated_bench. They are a process-level replay of counters, not a cross-host or timing replication. The README states the other limits: one host class, one size (n53), one params file.

F8 (binary provenance). The ic price outputs record commit, software.git_commit and software.git_dirty as null. The binding of ic-baseline to d34b9b390 and ic-candidate to 6bc18857b rests on the study's statement and on arms.sha256, which was written from the first session's binaries (file mtimes 2026-10-23 01:02 and 00:57 UTC, after 6bc18857b at 00:52:04 UTC). I did not rebuild them, because of the disk and CPU limits. What I verified: both files' sha256 equal arms.sha256; each file's BLAKE3, computed with the upstream C reference implementation (blake3 1.8.7, portable build, from the local cargo registry), equals software.binary_blake3 in every recorded and replayed output of its arm (a and q: 5813db98…, c: 7893f90c…); and the two files differ.

F9 (scope of the identity claim). The README says 'Every counted operation is identical between arms, so GAE records and every IC row's counted columns stand'. Here identity is verified for rule v3 k0n53/T01 only: all counters, relation counts, status and the recovered logarithm agree across 126 recorded and 6 replayed processes, both arms. Other rows are covered only by the code argument (same summands in the same order) and the first session's unit test and n61 identity check, which were not re-run here.

F10 (timeline and schedule). PROTOCOL.md, run.sh and arms.sha256 were committed at 14:25:49 UTC (5d726412b). The first process started at 14:26:31 UTC, and none of those files changed afterwards. summarise.sh was committed at 14:28:46 UTC (57b9de782), after the first process and before the last (15:00:07). It implements what PROTOCOL.md declared, so this is an ordering note only. All 126 processes started in the declared order: rounds 1 to 42, each in permutation (r-1) mod 6. Every isolation record's command names the declared binary for its label, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, the declared params path and its own --out file.

F11 (independence disclosure). This validator is a subagent launched from the Claude Code session whose URL appears in the trailers of the change commit (6bc18857b) and of every aa2 commit. It wrote its own reduction in Python, did not execute summarise.sh, and imports no repository code. It read the study's files, the params, the registry and the hash-to-curve definition in src/bin/ic/workflow.rs, which it re-implemented with its own BLAKE3, and it did not see the producer's transcript. The independence is in code and context, not organisational; a validator from another session would be stronger.

F12 (claim class). The change is correctly classed as engineering. It moves no counted cost: S and every IC row's gap to the matched rho are unchanged, and the board's rule v7 row for this curve is not re-priced. The established effect is about 8.5% less collect-phase time (1/1.093) on one host. The gate's matched-rho reference with the §5a band, required in VALIDATION.json, is outside this report.

F13 (HEAD moved during validation). The worktree was at f072a62bb when validation began and is at 5190fd62d4 now (5190fd62d: leaderboard files and scripts/build_ic_leaderboard.py only). research/ic_aimed_gather_20261023 is byte-identical between the two commits (git diff --quiet), so the validated snapshot is the committed study at either commit.

F14 (the rendered board is stale). scripts/build_ic_leaderboard.py was changed in 7a1b8112e, but docs/ic/LEADERBOARD.md, docs/ic-leaderboard.html and docs/ic/leaderboard.json were not regenerated. As committed, they show the as-run intervals under the label 'median [95% bootstrap]', and the verdict 'not established' for the whole set-up without the 'marginal' marking. They also show the section as not validated, so no validated display of the wrong intervals exists. Regenerating them is needed before or with VALIDATION.json; the builder derives the standing from that file in any case.

F15 (the first session's publications are not annotated). research/ic_aimed_gather_20261023/README.md and report/report.typ (and its PDF) still give the as-run 30-round intervals as the result: collect [1.065, 1.160], whole set-up [1.018, 1.068], and '1.065 against 1.087'. The verdict does not change (corrected collect lower end 1.082 < A/A upper end 1.087, margin -0.005), but those intervals are wrong in the same way. A one-line pointer to aa2_20261029/CORRECTION.md would close it. The first session's records and summary.json should stay as they are.

F16 (what the corrected generator is). Modulo 2^31, the LCG's lowest bit alternates. With n even, every resample of n consecutive draws therefore contains exactly n/2 odd-numbered and n/2 even-numbered rounds: 21/21 in all 2000 resamples at n = 42, and 15/15 at n = 30. The corrected interval is thus a parity-stratified percentile bootstrap, not an iid one. In aa2 the parity strata are the two halves of the schedule. Against an iid Mersenne-Twister reference (400,000 resamples), each bound moves by at most 0.0007 (collect A/B hi 1.1358 vs 1.1365; whole set-up A/A hi 1.0156 vs 1.0149) and no verdict changes. Labelling the corrected intervals '95% bootstrap' is accurate to that precision; this is a note, not a defect.

F17 (correct_bootstrap.sh does not re-apply the drop rule). It takes every round as kept instead of dropping rounds with a contended or failed process, as PROTOCOL.md and ../PROTOCOL.md require. This is harmless here: 0 of 126 (aa2) and 0 of 70 (first session) isolation records are contended or nonzero-exit. It would matter only if the script were reused.

F18 (leaderboard text, minor). The section text in both renderers says 'Every arm counts the same operations and recovers the same logarithm'; adding 'on the measured params' would match the corrected README. The verdict logic itself is right: 'established' only when both generators agree, 'marginal (+m), not claimed' when only the corrected one does, otherwise 'not established'.

F19 (wording checked and accurate). Checked against the recompute and accurate: CORRECTION.md ('confirmed before any result was shown as validated'; the board showed the section as not validated); 'Medians, counts, identity and isolation figures are unaffected: only the intervals are' (and the established flags that follow from them); README 'clears the A/A's 1.016 by 0.005' (+0.0047, rounded); report.typ 'an independent replay matched every non-timing field in both arms'. Also accurate: the 'not claimed' framing of the whole set-up in all three documents.
limitations: No rebuild of the binaries from d34b9b390 and 6bc18857b (disk and CPU limits); provenance as in F8.
No timing replication: the replays are sequential and unisolated, and their times are informational only.
The matched rho reference and the §5a band required by VALIDATION.json are not assessed here.

The scalar check depends on the registry's G and modulus and on the target derivation documented in src/bin/ic/workflow.rs (re-implemented, not imported); the derived Q equals the independently recorded Q.
